Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question by pressing star then one again. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides Voltara Motors has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in raw material sourcing and cost management, capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, battery costs per kWh and trends, total vehicle deliveries volume, strategic outlook and priorities for the next quarter and year, gross margin percentage and trends, updates on supply chain constraints and mitigation strategies, and energy business revenue and profitability. The market reception to our V8 truck has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated production ramp and demand surge far exceeding our initial estimates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q3 reached $7.2 billion, marking an exceptional 45% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin expanded to 22.3%, driven by enhanced operational efficiencies and a favorable product mix. Operating expenses amounted to $1.8 billion, resulting in a net income of $450 million. Our financial position remains strong, with $4.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We anticipate revenue of $8.0 to $8.5 billion for the upcoming quarter.

As we dive deeper into our Q3 results, I'd like to spend some time on raw material sourcing and cost management—a critical driver of our gross margins, which expanded 420 basis points year-over-year. In the EV space, where battery materials alone account for roughly 45% of the bill of materials for our flagship V8 EV SUV and V6 compact crossover, navigating commodity volatility, geopolitical risks, and supply constraints is paramount. We've made significant strides here, delivering a 15% sequential reduction in our weighted average cost per kWh for battery cells to $92/kWh, down from the $108/kWh peak in Q1 2023 amid the post-pandemic lithium correction.

Battery cathode and anode precursors remain the core battleground. Battery materials comprise 38% of total raw material costs, up from 32% two years ago as we scale production of our next-gen 4680-style cylindrical cells at our Nevada Gigafactory. Lithium carbonate equivalent prices, which spiked to $80,000 per metric ton in late 2022, have normalized to around $14,000/mt today—a 82% drawdown—thanks to surging supply from Australian hard-rock projects like Pilbara Minerals' Pilgangoora and new brine ramps in South America's Lithium Triangle. Our strategy has been proactive: We've locked in 70% of our 2024-2026 lithium needs via long-term offtake agreements with SQM and Albemarle at blended prices averaging $18,500/mt, shielding us from spot market whipsaws. This has contributed to a 22% YoY decline in our lithium-intensive NMC 811 cathode costs.

On nickel, critical for high-energy-density NHP chemistries, we've diversified away from volatile LME pricing—currently at $16,500/mt, down 40% from 2023 highs—by securing 60% of supply from low-cost Indonesian HPAL producers like Tsingshan and PT Halmahera Persada Lygend. This regional shift has cut our nickel sulfate costs by 28% YoY, despite Indonesia's evolving nickel ore export bans. Cobalt, a smaller but ESG-sensitive input at 5-7% of cathode mass, is sourced primarily from ethical DRC partners like Glencore's Katanga mine, with 50% hedged via futures to mitigate the 15% price dip to $28,000/mt. Looking ahead, we're accelerating our LFP cathode adoption—now 25% of our Shanghai Gigafactory output in partnership with CATL—targeting zero-cobalt formulations that reduce material costs by 20-25% per kWh while enhancing supply security.

For anodes, synthetic graphite pricing has stabilized at $8,500/mt after a 35% correction, but we've invested $250 million in a JV with Group14 Technologies for silicon-carbon composites, aiming to boost energy density by 15% and cut graphite reliance by 30% by 2026.

Beyond batteries, chassis and powertrain materials make up 25% of our cost base. Hot-rolled coil steel prices have hovered at $650/mt globally, pressured by overcapacity in China, but our advanced high-strength steel sourcing from ArcelorMittal's U.S. mills—under a 5-year LTA—has held our per-vehicle steel costs flat YoY at $1,200/unit. Aluminum, key for our die-cast gigacastings inspired by Giga Press tech, saw LME prices dip to $2,200/mt; we've optimized via recycling partnerships with Novelis, recovering 40% of our scrap aluminum and slashing virgin primary costs by 18%.

Copper, essential for motors and inverters, represents a growing pain point at $9,200/mt amid supply tightness from Codelco and Freeport disruptions. Our exposure is $450 per vehicle, up 12% YoY, but we've launched a $100 million copper recycling initiative at our Berlin Gigafactory, targeting 25% recycled content by 2025, and are hedging 40% of 2024 needs on the LME.

Geopolitically, we've reduced China dependency from 55% in 2021 to 32% today, with North America now at 28% (up from 18%), Europe at 25%, and Australia/Indonesia at 15%. This friendshoring aligns with IRA incentives, qualifying us for $7.5 billion in battery production tax credits through localized sourcing—e.g., our LFP cells from AESC in Tennessee using U.S./Australian lithium. In Europe, we're compliant with the Critical Raw Materials Act via LTAs with Northvolt for precursor production. Supply chain resilience includes dual-sourcing 85% of Tier 1 battery suppliers like LGES, Panasonic, and CATL, and maintaining 90-day strategic inventories, which buffered us through Red Sea disruptions.

Innovation is key: Our in-house dry electrode coating process, rolled out at scale in Q3, eliminates solvents and cuts cell manufacturing costs by 15%, indirectly lowering raw material intensity. We've also deployed AI-driven predictive analytics—powered by our SAP/Blackline ERP integration—to forecast commodity curves with 92% accuracy, enabling dynamic hedging. Recycling yields are ramping: Our Redwood Materials partnership processed 12,000 tonnes of black mass in Q3, recovering 95% lithium and 98% nickel/cobalt at 60% below virgin costs.

Structurally, the EV raw materials market is inflecting: McKinsey projects lithium supply to grow 3x to 3.5 Mt LCE by 2030, easing deficits, while nickel and copper face 20-30% shortages without accelerated mining capex. Our capex plan allocates $2.2 billion—or 28% of total 2024 capex—to vertical integration, including a $1.5 billion cathode precursor plant in South Carolina. This positions us for sustained margin expansion: We guide to battery costs falling to $75/kWh by year-end 2024 and $60/kWh by 2026, supporting ASPs above $45,000. Risks remain—e.g., potential U.S. tariffs on Indonesian nickel or EU CBAM carbon border taxes—but our playbook is robust. Overall, raw material cost management drove 60% of our Q3 margin beat, underscoring our competitive moat.

Turning to our capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, which remain the cornerstone of our strategy to scale Voltara Motors into a global EV powerhouse. The EV market is at an inflection point: global EV sales hit 14 million units in 2023, up 35% year-over-year, driven by falling battery costs—now averaging $132 per kWh, a 20% drop from last year—and supportive policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act's $7,500 consumer tax credit and 45X manufacturing credits. But with Chinese OEMs like BYD flooding affordable segments and legacy players like Ford and GM ramping Ultium and Model e platforms, we're laser-focused on execution to capture 5% global market share by 2027.

For FY24, we're guiding CapEx to $6.8 billion, up 15% from $5.9 billion in FY23, with a forward outlook of $25-30 billion over the next three years. This represents about 25% of our projected FY24 revenue of $28 billion, in line with peers like Tesla's 20-25% CapEx-to-revenue ratio during their growth phase. We've optimized our spend through a disciplined ROI framework, targeting projects with IRRs above 20% and paybacks under 4 years, leveraging IRA incentives that could unlock up to $1.2 billion in credits.

Our top priority is manufacturing capacity expansion, 45% of FY24 CapEx at ~$3.1 billion. We're investing $2.2 billion in our new Gigafactory Texas Phase 2, bringing annual output to 500 GWh by 2026—ramping from 150 GWh today. This mirrors Tesla's Texas Gigafactory playbook but with 40% dedicated to structural battery packs using our in-house 46-series cylindrical cells, reducing pack costs by 18% versus LFP prismatic alternatives.

Regionally, in North America, $800 million to retrofit our Spartanburg, South Carolina plant for 200,000 units of V8 truck production, qualifying for $400 million in IRA advanced manufacturing credits. In Europe, $500 million goes to our Berlin-Brandenburg JV with a European partner to localize V6 assembly, dodging the EU's 10% import tariffs on Chinese EVs and targeting 100,000 units for the 2025 EBA mandate compliance. Asia-Pacific gets $300 million for supplier localization in India and Southeast Asia, hedging against U.S.-China trade tensions and tapping into a market where EV penetration is still sub-5% but growing 50% YoY.

Battery technology and vertical integration take 30% of FY24 CapEx at ~$2.0 billion. Battery margins are make-or-break—raw materials like cathode precursors are down 25% YoY, but supply chain bottlenecks persist. We're doubling down on vertical integration, investing $1.4 billion in cell-to-pack production at Gigafactory Nevada. Key initiatives include $900 million to scale 4680 cell dry electrode ramp from 10 GWh pilot to 100 GWh, achieving 16% energy density gains over 2170 cells, with silicon-doped anodes for 20% faster charging (10-80% in 18 minutes on 350 kW DC). $500 million for lithium manganese-rich cathodes, targeting $80/kWh packs by 2027, and early-stage solid-state prototypes with sulfide electrolytes for 600-mile range. We're securing 80% of our lithium via U.S. and Australian offtakes, reducing exposure to Congo DRC cobalt risks.

Autonomy, software, and charging ecosystem get 15% of CapEx at ~$1.0 billion. Software-defined vehicles are the next frontier. $600 million on our Apex Autonomy stack: Level 3 highway autonomy in V8 trucks by Q4 2025, with 10 billion miles of synthetic data training via NVIDIA DGX clusters. Robotaxi pilots in Austin and Shanghai will consume $200 million, aiming for unsupervised FSD by 2027. On charging, $400 million builds 5,000 DC fast chargers across NACS-standard corridors, partnering with Electrify America, supporting our 95% uptime SLA.

Supply chain resilience and sustainability take 10% of CapEx at ~$700 million: $400 million for rare earth magnet localization in Texas—critical for PM motors amid China's 90% dominance—and $300 million for recycled battery hubs, targeting 30% circularity by 2028 per EU Battery Regulation.

These investments drive 25% YoY cost reductions through 2026, targeting AEB parity at $25,000 for our V4 compact by 2026. Risks like semiconductor shortages and interest rates—we've hedged 70% of chip needs with TSMC and locked 80% debt at sub-5% via green bonds. Flex CapEx is 20% toggleable if demand softens. In summary, our CapEx is fueling a 50% production ramp to 1.2 million units in 2025, with EBITDA margins expanding to 15% by FY26.

Let's focus on battery costs per kWh, a pivotal line item accounting for roughly 35% of our vehicle BOM. Our disciplined execution has unlocked over $1.2 billion in year-to-date cost savings. In Q3 2024, our average lithium-ion battery pack cost landed at $112 per kWh, a 15% sequential decline from Q1's $132/kWh and 18% better than Q2 2023's $137/kWh. This puts us on track for full-year guidance of $105-108/kWh, ahead of the BloombergNEF industry average of $118/kWh. At the cell level, we're procuring at a blended average of $68/kWh, reflecting a mix of NMC 811 cathodes for our premium V8 and LFP cells for our mass-market V6 lineup.

The trajectory shows an 18% CAGR decline since 2022, outpacing the industry's 14% benchmark. Powered by raw material deflation, manufacturing yield improvements, and chemistry transitions. Lithium carbonate spot prices cratered 82% from 2022 peaks to $15/kg, thanks to Australian and South American oversupply. Nickel sulfate down 45% YoY, cobalt mitigated via supplier mix. We've locked 80% of 2025 volumes via long-term offtakes with Ganfeng and Albemarle.

Our Nevada Gigafactory 2 runs at 85% OEE, with 4680 cylindrical cells yielding 92% first-pass efficiency. $450 million in dry electrode coating slashes solvent costs by 30%, enabling 20% higher energy density. Partnering with CATL on LFP packs at $56/kWh cell costs, now 55% of output. This saved $18/kWh on our entry-level SUV, boosting range to 320 miles EPA.

Regionally, China hits sub-$50/kWh on LFP, Europe $75/kWh equivalent post-CBAM, US benefits from IRA $40/kWh effective subsidy. We've localized 70% stateside. At $112/kWh, our V8 achieves a 52% pack-to-vehicle cost ratio. Passing 40% savings to ASPs at $48,500, banking rest for 32% full-year margins. Vertical integration targets $70/kWh by 2026 with silicon-dominant anodes. Recycling cuts virgin costs 25% by 2027. Risks like lithium rebound derisked by hedging and sodium-ion R&D.

Now, on total vehicle deliveries: In Q3 2024, Voltara delivered a record 185,432 vehicles globally, a 28% YoY increase from 144,800 units in Q3 2023, and 12% sequential growth from 165,500 in Q2. This underscores our ramps at Gigafactory Nevada and Berlin, over 95% utilization on V6 and V8 lines.

By model: V6 sedan, 78,200 units up 32% YoY, fueled by Long Range variant and 12,000 fleet orders from Uber. V8 crossover bestseller, 92,500 units up 26% YoY, OTA updates unlocking FSD Beta, 15,000 Performance AWD. V8 truck ramped to 12,300 units, tripling YoY. Premium V1 sedan 2,432 units, ASPs $105,000+.

Regionally: North America 112,400 units (61%), up 35% YoY, IRA incentives, 28% leases. Europe 42,100 (23%), up 22% YoY, Berlin localization. Asia-Pacific 27,900 (15%), up 40% QoQ on Shanghai JV.

EV mix 98%, inventory 18 days. Q4 guidance 210,000-230,000 deliveries. Validating Ramp to 1 Million, AI robotics boosting speeds 20%.

Gross margin performance: Consolidated automotive gross margin 18.7% excluding credits, up 630 bps YoY from 12.4%, 150 bps sequential. Including $45 million credits, 20.1%.

Volume and efficiency +420 bps: 128,000 deliveries up 61% YoY, revenue $2.8B up 52%, COGS/vehicle $41,200 down 15%, 92% utilization.

Mix and ASP +180 bps: Premium trims 42%, ASP $52,400 steady.

COGS reductions +320 bps: Battery $85/kWh down 28%, IRA $320M credits, cell-to-chassis cuts 30% weight.

Credits +140 bps, up 40% YoY.

Regional: NA 22.5%, Europe 14.2%, APAC 19.8%. Q3 guide 22-24%, mid-20s year-end.

On supply chain constraints: We've navigated semiconductor shortages (12% YoY contraction), deferring 22,000 units, lithium spikes shaving 150 bps margins. Asia lead times extended, Europe port issues.

Mitigations: Reduced single-supplier to 15%, 3-2-1 model. TSMC offtakes for SiC, inventory 85 days. Nevada Gigafactory 20 GWh, 40% US LFP, 10-year lithium contracts. BHP nickel PPA, LFP 55%. Dynamic routing, AI Control Tower 98.5% OTIF. Mexico expansion for 30 GWh. Q3 drag eases to 5-7%.

Finally, energy business: $2.3B revenue, 112% YoY up from $1.08B, 22% sequential, 18% total revenue. Grid-scale $1.43B (62%), 6.2 GWh deployments, TeraVault wins with PG&E, Enel. Residential $650M, 285,000 HomeVaults. Solar/services $220M.

Margin 29.8%, up 450 bps YoY. Cell transition $112/kWh, 92% utilization, EBITDA $785M 34% margin. NA 55%, EMEA 25%, APAC 18%. Q4 $2.7-3.0B 30-32% margins, $14.5B backlog.

Next, we'll hear from Dr. Liam Chen regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, including AI-optimized robotics and gigacasting at 9,000-ton presses, resulting in increased production output—now at 95% utilization across Nevada and Berlin—reduced cycle times by 20%, and first-pass yields up to 92% on 4680 lines. Our Spartanburg retrofit and Texas Phase 2 are on track for 500 GWh by 2026, with structural packs cutting assembly time significantly.

Following me, Sophia Grant will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, like silicon-anode pilots and LMR cathodes for $80/kWh packs; autonomous driving systems, with Apex stack for Level 3+ on 10,000 units; and vehicle connectivity via weekly OTA updates and V2G/VPP integration. We're committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions—like 600-mile solid-state prototypes and end-to-end neural nets—that will redefine the future of mobility, monetizing software at 45% margins.

After me, Raj Patel will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network—reducing China to 32%, friendshoring to 28% NA—to mitigate risks and ensure seamless material flow. Our proactive approach, including 90-day inventories, dual-sourcing 85% Tier 1s, AI predictive analytics at 92% accuracy, and blockchain traceability, has enabled us to navigate global challenges like Red Sea disruptions and semi shortages effectively. Mexico Gigafactory adds USMCA-compliant capacity.

Next, Jordan Lee will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth, with 185k deliveries, ASPs at $48,200, and strong demand across regions—35% YoY NA growth, UK +45%. We're actively pursuing new opportunities like India/Brazil CKD kits, fleet wins with Hertz/Uber, and premium trims at 42% mix, while our direct model and software upsells maintain pricing power.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. We'll pause for a moment to assemble the queue.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the raw material cost trends, particularly lithium and nickel hedging, and how that flows into 2025 margins?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question. As Marcus detailed, our LTAs lock 70% lithium at $18,500/mt blended and 60% nickel from Indonesian HPAL, driving 22% cathode cost declines. This, plus LFP ramp and recycling, supports battery costs to $75/kWh YE24, flowing 600bps to margins for mid-20s in 2025.

Analyst 2:
Great, follow-up on capex—how flexible is the $6.8B FY24 guide if EV demand softens further?

Marcus Hale:
Solid question. 20% is flex CapEx, toggleable like Rivian did. We've got ROI gates above 20% IRR, IRA unlocks $1.2B credits, and demand signals strong with V8 reservations converting 65%. We're confident in the $25-30B 3-year plan for 1.2M unit ramp.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. On manufacturing, with Gigafactory Texas Phase 2, what's the timeline for 500 GWh and any bottlenecks?

Dr. Liam Chen:
Phase 2 breaks ground Q4, full ramp by 2026. Bottlenecks were cell yields, now 92% on dry electrode lines. Automation and structural packs de-risk, targeting 1,200 units/week per line.

Analyst 4:
For battery costs, how does $112/kWh compare to Tesla and CATL, and silicon anode progress?

Sophia Grant:
Our pack-level beats BNEF average, cell $68/kWh competitive with Tesla Shanghai ~$96/kWh, ahead of LG. Silicon pilots at 15% Q2 production next year, 15-20% density boost validated with Argonne.

Analyst 5:
Supply chain-wise, with Red Sea ongoing, how's inventory buffering and Mexico impact?

Raj Patel:
90-day strategic stocks buffered fully, dynamic routing via FourKites cut variances 25%. Mexico 30 GWh by 2025 captures IRA bonuses, nearshoring 85% localization.

Analyst 6:
Sales question: Regional mix shift, especially APAC pricing pressure from BYD—any ASP erosion guide?

Jordan Lee:
APAC up 40% QoQ despite BYD, ASP stable via software edge, 20% lower TCO. Full-year ASP $48-52k, mix to high-margin V8 SUV 35%.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:
On energy business, $2.3B beat—backlog details and VPP revenue potential?

Elena Vasquez:
$14.5B backlog, 70% grid-scale like PG&E 15 GWh. VPP via Autobidder-like software hit $45M ancillary in ERCOT, V2G pilots unlock $100M+ by 2026.

Analyst 8:
Gross margin guide to mid-20s—what's the biggest lever, and regulatory credit sustainability?

Marcus Hale:
Volume leverage and COGS cuts (battery 28% down) primary, 420 bps from scale. Credits $30-50M/quarter moderate but high-margin buffer as market saturates.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. As we look ahead, our priorities remain accelerating production scale, unlocking tech leadership, and regional expansion—targeting Q1 2025 deliveries 65-70k, FY25 350-380k, EBITDA 18-20%, positive FCF $1.2-1.5B. We're confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
